procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay and High Court of Allahabad
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 07.03.2013 of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay in ITA No. 2134 of 2012 and Income Tax Appeal No. 224 of 2014 decided by High Court of Allahabad
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Judicature at Bombay issued a Judgment and Order dated 07.03.2013 in ITA No. 2134 of 2012. The High Court of Allahabad decided Income Tax Appeal No. 224 of 2014.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The Appellant(s) appealed to the Supreme Court, which dismissed the appeals.

issue.issue_text: Whether the view of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), as affirmed by the High Court, is correct.

facts: The case is an appeal from a judgment of the High Court of Judicature at Bombay, which had affirmed a decision by the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).
The counsel for the Revenue argued in favor of a view taken by the Assessing Officer (AO), submitting that this view was consistently supported by a series of judicial pronouncements.
law: The court considered several previous judgments cited in support of the Revenue's argument, including:
- Servo-Med Industries Private Limited v. Commissioner of Central Excise, Mumbai
- Commissioner of Income Tax, Kerala v. Tara Agencies
- Commissioner of Income Tax, Madras v. Vinbros and Company (2015) 14 SCC 483
application: The Supreme Court evaluated the arguments and the supporting case law presented by the parties.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the view taken by the ITAT and subsequently affirmed by the High Court was correct. As a result, the Court found no merit in the appeals and dismissed them.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the view of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), as affirmed by the High Court, is correct.
appellant_arguments: The view of the Assessing Officer (AO) was correct and has been consistently taken in a series of judicial pronouncements.
Relied on judgments such as Servo-Med Industries Private Limited v. Commissioner of Central Excise and Commissioner of Income Tax, Kerala v. Tara Agencies to support their contention.
respondent_arguments: The findings of the Tribunal, as upheld by the High Court, were correct and there was no question of law involved.
Cited judgments from other High Courts which held that LPG bottling amounts to manufacture, and pointed out that the Department had not appealed those decisions.
Argued that the judgments relied upon by the Revenue, such as the Kosan Gas Company case, were distinguishable and not applicable.

cases.case_name: Commissioner of Income Tax, Madras v. Vinbros and Company

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The provisions of the relevant Act utilize the expression 'manufacture'.
obiter: The view of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) as affirmed by the High Court is correct.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: In our view, applying the tests laid down by this Court in Sesa Goa case [(2004) 13 sec 548 : (2004) 271 ITR 331] and applying it to the activities undertaken by the respondents herein, reproduced hereinabove, it is clear that the said activities would come within the meaning of the word "production".
legal_tests_applied: The test of 'manufacture' propounded on that case would not be applicable when dealing with the cases under the provisions of Sections 80HH, 80-1 and 80-lA of the Act which use both the expressions 'manufacture' and 'production'.
The tests laid down by this Court in Sesa Goa case [(2004) 13 sec 548 : (2004) 271 ITR 331].
why_appellant_lost: Judgment in the cases of Servo-Med Industries Private Limited and Tara Agencies, which were cited by the learned counsel for the Revenue, may not apply to the present case.

They dealt with the provision of the Central Excise Act and, therefore, test of 'manufacture' propounded on that case would not be applicable when dealing with the cases under the provisions of Sections 80HH, 80-1 and 80-lA of the Act which use both the expressions 'manufacture' and 'production'.
why_respondent_won: The view of the !TAT as affirmed by the High Court is correct.
The activities undertaken by the respondents would come within the meaning of the word 'production' when applying the tests from the Sesa Goa case.
The ITAT correctly found that the LPG produced in the refinery cannot be directly supplied to the consumer for domestic use because of various reasons of handling, storage and safety.
